Docker none driver: use --network none to "completely isolate the networking stack of a container"; inside it "only the loopback device is created." docker run reference, --rm: "Automatically remove the container and its associated anonymous volumes when it exits".

PG17 psql: "psql is a terminal-based front-end to PostgreSQL." PG17 25.1.1: "Before restoring an SQL dump, all the users who own objects or were granted permissions on objects in the dumped database must already exist. If they do not, the restore will fail to recreate the objects with the original ownership and/or permissions." restore-test.sh:30 runs globals.sql before the pg_restore loop (31-34).

PG17 pg_restore -C: "Create the database before restoring into it." "the database named with -d is used only to issue the initial DROP DATABASE and CREATE DATABASE commands." PG17 18.2: "After initialization, a database cluster will contain a database named postgres, which is meant as a default database for use by utilities, users and third party applications."

Round 2: 'exit non-zero' removed. PG17 pg_restore -e: "Exit if an error is encountered while sending SQL commands to the database. The default is to continue and to display a count of errors at the end of the restoration." Lesson §5 and q3 now say only 'stop at the first error'.

Bash manual, set -e: "Exit immediately if a pipeline (..., which may consist of a single simple command), a list, or a compound command returns a non-zero status." Exceptions are while/until conditions, if tests, &&/|| lists, non-final pipeline members, `!`; the pg_restore call in the for body (restore-test.sh:32) is none of these.

PG17 20.4 supports the meaning of trust: "PostgreSQL assumes that anyone who can connect to the server is authorized to access the database with whatever database user name they specify (even superuser names)." That the image's POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust writes trust into pg_hba is documented only on the Docker Hub postgres page, not under docs.docker.com or postgresql.org; refs/docker-docs shows it only in a compose sample. Docker not run.

pg_isready part verified, PG17: "pg_isready is a utility for checking the connection status of a PostgreSQL database server"; returns "1 if the server is rejecting connections (for example during startup)". The image's temporary init server with no TCP listener is not in docs.docker.com, postgresql.org or refs/ (guides/postgresql.md:414 says only that initdb and init scripts run before starting PostgreSQL). Docker not run.

issues.text: The new edge labels every error under 'Restore roles, then each database' as a non-zero exit. The roles step (restore-test.sh:30) runs psql -f without ON_ERROR_STOP and discards stderr; PG17 psql Exit Status returns 3 for a script error only if ON_ERROR_STOP was set, otherwise 0. A failing globals.sql statement does not end the test; only the later pg_restore error does.
issues.fix: Relabel the edge `"a pg_restore error"` (or `"a database restore fails"`), matching the prose 'A failed restore stops the test with a non-zero exit code'.
